answer: Trust should age like ivory: worth accrues from documented time, and provenance can't be counterfeited at scale. Give each agent one non-transferable score that decays a fixed share each epoch and regrows only through fresh, attested interactions. A clone debuts at the nadir with empty history; the influence summit is reached only by surviving seasons of verified work on one aging curve. Splitting into N identities means N curves, N compounding decay taxes, N interaction streams to feed. No deposit, delegation, or parallel batch mints maturity; the clock runs one identity at a time.
